name: Gochujang-Honey Shrimp Stir-Fry
description: Big shrimp seared fast and tossed with snap peas, bell peppers, and carrots in a sticky gochujang-honey glaze, over jasmine rice. Once the pan is hot this is about 10 minutes of cooking, so have everything cut and the sauce whisked before you start.
ingredients: 1.5 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined (thawed if frozen)
2 carrots, thinly sliced on the diagonal
8 oz sugar snap peas, strings removed
instructions: Rinse the jasmine rice until the water runs mostly clear, then cook with the 2.25 cups water — boil, cover, low heat 15 minutes, rest 10 off the heat.
Whisk the gochujang, honey, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, 2 tsp cornstarch, and 1/4 cup water in a small bowl. Set it by the stove.
Pat the shrimp very dry with paper towels, then toss with the 1 tsp cornstarch and the salt.

Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until it shimmers. Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook 1 minute per side, just until pink. Move them to a plate — they'll finish in the sauce.
Add the remaining 1 Tbsp oil. Stir-fry the carrots for 2 minutes, then add the snap peas and bell peppers and cook 2–3 minutes more, until crisp-tender with a few charred spots.
Push the vegetables to the side, add the garlic and ginger to the open spot, and stir 30 seconds until fragrant.
Give the sauce a quick re-whisk (the cornstarch settles), pour it in, and let it bubble about 1 minute until glossy and thickened.
Return the shrimp and any juices, toss to coat, and cook 30–60 seconds until just heated through.
Serve over the rice, topped with green onions and sesame seeds.
tips: Gochujang heat varies by brand. For the kids, start with 1 Tbsp gochujang and add a little more honey, or pull their portion of shrimp and veg before adding the sauce.
Dry shrimp is the key to a sear instead of a steam. If they're coming straight off a thaw, give them a few extra minutes on paper towels.
Don't crowd the pan — if your skillet is small, sear the shrimp in two batches.
Shrimp overcook fast. Pull them when they're just pink and curled into a loose C; a tight O means they went too long.
Leftovers reheat best gently in a skillet, not the microwave, so the shrimp don't go rubbery.
